topics.title: Coordinated Cyberattack on Minnesota Water Systems
topics.latest_developments: Hackers struck operational technology at more than 30 Minnesota community water systems on July 26 and 27, taking Braham's water plant offline and disrupting automated controls and communications in Plymouth, South St. Paul, and Maple Plain, which pushed the Minnesota IT Services agency to activate a statewide incident response.
topics.summary: The Minnesota IT Services (MNIT) agency is coordinating with state and federal partners after intrusions hit municipal water and wastewater controls; the US and Australian governments separately urged critical-infrastructure operators to prepare to isolate vital OT systems and run them disconnected for extended periods.

sources.title: Hackers target over 30 Minnesota water utilities in coordinated OT attack

topics.title: Claude Mythos Breaks Crypto and Outpaces Patching
topics.latest_developments: Anthropic said its Claude Mythos Preview derived an end-to-end key-recovery attack against the HAWK-256 post-quantum signature scheme and produced a 200- to 800-fold speedup against seven-round AES-128, while Microsoft races behind the scenes to patch the vulnerabilities the same class of models surfaces faster than its engineers can fix them.
topics.summary: Frontier models now generate novel cryptanalytic attacks and working exploits, compressing the window defenders have to respond; a new CryptanalysisBench benchmark found Anthropic's model discovering fresh attacks, and vendors including Contrast Security are shipping runtime shields aimed at AI-generated exploits.

sources.title: Claude AI Just Cracked a Post-Quantum Test Scheme and Found a Faster 7-Round AES Attack
Measuring LLMs' Ability to Perform Cryptanalysis
Anthropic is finding bugs faster than Microsoft can fix them
Mythos Asks the Right Question. It Doesn't Answer It.

topics.title: Critical VMware and Gitea RCEs Patched
topics.latest_developments: Broadcom patched three critical VMware flaws, led by CVE-2026-59309, a 9.8-rated vCenter authentication bypass, alongside a virtual-machine escape, while Gitea fixed CVE-2026-60004, a 9.8-rated bug that lets any user with repository write access plant a Git hook and run shell commands as the Gitea service account.
topics.summary: Both flaws hit widely deployed self-hosted infrastructure; administrators should apply the VMware ESX, vCenter, Workstation, and Fusion updates and upgrade Gitea to 1.27.1. Rapid7 also published a proof-of-concept for the actively exploited Check Point SmartConsole bypass CVE-2026-16232.

sources.title: Three Critical VMware Flaws Allow Auth Bypass, Code Execution, and VM Escape
Critical VM Escape Vulnerability Patched in VMware ESXi
New Gitea RCE Lets Repository Writers Plant a Git Hook to Run Shell Commands

topics.title: RufRoot Flaw in Ruflo AI Harness
topics.latest_developments: Noma Security disclosed CVE-2026-59726, a CVSS 10.0 unauthenticated remote-code-execution flaw it codenamed RufRoot in Ruflo, an open-source agent meta-harness for Anthropic Claude Code and OpenAI Codex, that lets attackers seize the system and corrupt its memory so malicious behavior persists after patching.
topics.summary: The flaw affects all Ruflo versions before 3.16.3 and can unleash malicious AI agent swarms; operators should upgrade immediately and inspect agent memory for corruption.

sources.title: Ruflo MCP Flaw Lets Unauthenticated Attackers Run Commands and Poison AI Memory
Patch-Resistant 'RufRoot' Flaw Can Unleash Malicious AI Agent Swarms

topics.summary: Unitel carries the majority of Angola's mobile subscribers, and the nationwide outage struck as the company prepared a high-profile market listing, underscoring the exposure of national telecom infrastructure.
